items.heading: Ask Most Science Students What
items.text: Ask most science students what comes after their degree and you get one answer: MSc, in the same subject, at whichever college will take them.

items.heading: Eight Routes, Compared on Real
items.text: Eight routes, compared on real entry requirements, real time, and real outcomes. Compare all of them before you shortlist anything by subject in the next sections.

items.heading: Physics Has the Clearest Fork
items.text: Physics has the clearest fork of any subject on this list: a well-funded research path, or a quantitative pivot into industry.

rows: MSc (Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences, Maths, Statistics)
IIT JAM, CUET PG, or university-specific test; bachelor's degree in the subject, usually 50%+ aggregate
Feeds into CSIR-NET/JRF, PhD, teaching, or a certification pivot. Rarely a direct high-salary route by itself.
M.Tech in an interdisciplinary department (for MSc holders)
step score in the relevant paper (Physics, Chemistry, Maths, Life Sciences); offered at select IITs in applied physics, instrumentation, nanoscience, or materials science
A narrower option than a standard engineering M.Tech, but genuinely opens R&D and core-industry roles that a plain MSc does not.
CSIR-NET JRF, step, or JEST (Physics); Integrated PhD at IISc, TIFR, IISERs after a bachelor's degree
4-6 years for a standalone PhD; 5-6 years for an Integrated PhD after a bachelor's degree
Rs 37,000-42,000/month stipend on a CSIR/UGC fellowship; Rs 70,000-80,000/month under PMRF at top institutes. Leads to research, academia, or R&D roles.
CAT, XAT, CMAT, or GMAT; open to any bachelor's degree, science included
Institute-dependent. Strong institutes place science graduates into consulting, product, and analytics roles; weak institutes rarely beat a solid MSc plus certification.

visuals.heading: A Phd That Pays

figures.label: Education Budget
figures.source: A PhD that pays a Rs 42,000/month stipend and leads to a research career is not automatically worse than an MBA that costs Rs 15 lakh, if research genuinely fits how you want to spend the next several years. The reverse is just as true. The real question is which route fits your specific subject, your financial runway, and how fast you need income, not which one sounds the most respectable.
